stem: An adult client has progressive enlargement of the hands and feet with coarse facial features. Which disorder should the nurse suspect?
rationale: The Endocrine Society describes acromegaly as a disorder caused by excess growth hormone and notes that adults with acromegaly commonly have large hands and feet and coarse facial features. Therefore B is the best answer. The other endocrine disorders do not explain this characteristic pattern of progressive somatic overgrowth.
educational_objective: Recognize enlargement of the hands and feet with coarse facial features in an adult as a characteristic presentation of acromegaly.
source_locator: Introductory definition and section 'Symptoms and Risk Factors': acromegaly is caused by excess GH; common physical findings include large hands and feet and coarse facial features
source_claim_supported: In adults, acromegaly results from excess growth hormone and commonly produces enlargement of the hands and feet and coarse facial features.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Appendix A, Physiological Adaptation > Illness Management and Pathophysiology, printed p.48 / PDF p.52: apply knowledge of client pathophysiology to illness management; identify pathophysiology related to an acute or chronic condition
correction_summary: Removed the family-member narrative and the unsupported extra claim that the typical cause must be a pituitary tumor for purposes of answering the item. Reduced the stem to the characteristic source-supported adult somatic findings, rebuilt the alternatives as endocrine disorders within the same construct, added exact current source and NCSBN locators, and adjusted difficulty from hard to moderate.
audit_findings: B is directly supported by the Endocrine Society source. The stem tests recognition rather than definitive diagnosis and uses no unsupported laboratory thresholds or universal etiologic statement.
